Schnottz's Landing is a port recently built along the southwestern shores of Uldum. Commander Schnottz runs his operation from here, where his people loot the relics from the ancient temples in the region. These relics are being placed on their ships docked here. They invited the most illustrious figures of Azeroth to be present when they revealed the secrets of Uldum. Soon after the adventurer arrives, bad things start occurring at the camp. Ambassador Laurent is killed when he starts asking questions and Schnottz's bunker is blown up, with him inside. The invited guests are placed into the barracks and held against their will. After they manage to escape and Schnottz blames the adventurer

The scorpid are gigantic creatures similar to scorpions and arachnathid. They measure an average of 3 ft. long. They attack anything they perceive as a threat with their claws and stinger, which holds venom capable of killing creatures up to 100 times its own body weight. When stung, the venom causes rapid suffocation followed by violent seizures, and shortly after, death. Although tail venom of most scorpids is the most deadly, it is the bite of the diminutive scorpling that is the greatest threat. Some species also have venomous pincers. The Scourge Invasion was a world event in patch 1.11 that heralded the opening of Naxxramas, the citadel of the dreaded Kel'Thuzad. It was reintroduced into the game in patch 3.0.2 partway through the Zombie Infestation event, in preparation for Wrath of the Lich King, and tuned for the new level cap which players had achieved (70), occurring after Hallow's End. It is thus the only non-seasonal world event to have ever been repeated. Death Rising, the pre-event for Shadowlands as the Scourge are marauding across Azeroth, was heavily inspired by the Scourge Invasion.

Scott Mercer (alias Daelo) was the Lead Encounter Designer for World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King. He has worked at Blizzard Entertainment since 1997, first as a Level Designer for StarCraft and Warcraft III, followed by his later work on dungeon and raid encounters in World of Warcraft, eventually becoming the Lead Encounter Designer for the second expansion, Wrath of the Lich King.

Located in the Valley of Echoes, it gave them a path into Scourgeholme, which the highlord hoped to conquer and remake into an Argent Crusade fortress. Their first attack on Scourgeholme was initially successful, but they were quickly overrun and had to retreat back to Argent Vanguard. Scourgewar is the tenth normal World of Warcraft TCG set, released on 24 November, 2009. The icy shores of the frozen north welcome all those willing enough to enter. The ever-expanding reach of the Lich King has drawn the forces of both the Horde and the Alliance to the frigid lands of Northrend, but they do not know the horrors that await them. Can you muster the courage you will need when death itself stares back at you? The unrelenting forces of the Scourge have risen and they will stop at nothing until the last breath of life has been siphoned from Azeroth. The Scourgewar has begun...
